From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer review

## Executive assessment

The Seller’s update shifts several known transaction risks to Wattlebridge while restricting its ability to recover for them. The most important points are:

1. **Do not complete with Riverlark debt or security outstanding.** Repayment and discharge must occur at Completion through the funds flow.
2. **Make effective Bluefen consent a genuine Completion condition**, including satisfaction of its associated conditions—not merely receipt of a letter.
3. **Preserve meaningful remedies:** fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities should not be swept into the general 20% cap and 18-month deadline; fraud must be carved out expressly.
4. **Reject blanket data-room disclosure and “discoverable” buyer knowledge.** Known issues need targeted remedies where the Buyer is willing to proceed despite them.
5. **Resolve the Ironquay IP position and allocate the bonuses, incident and renewals expressly** before the price and Completion mechanics are finalised.

This review is based on the Seller’s summary and Disclosure Letter, not the complete SPA or underlying DD documents. The proposed drafting and the underlying records need to be checked together before agreement.

## 1. Liability, remedies and disclosure

### General warranty limitations

The proposed **AUD 4.8 million cap** is 20% of the AUD 24 million price. The 18-month notification period, AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 deductible basket further reduce practical recovery. The basket is not a “tipping” basket: even when qualifying claims exceed AUD 250,000, the first AUD 250,000 remains unrecoverable.

**Push back:** Seek a higher general cap, longer notification period, lower de minimis and a tipping basket. In particular, claims just below AUD 25,000 should not disappear from the aggregate basket without careful consideration. Confirm whether thresholds apply per individual matter or to related matters, how loss is calculated, and whether notice requirements are workable. The final figures are commercial negotiation points.

### Fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities

Applying the general cap and 18-month deadline to **title and capacity** is inappropriate for a purchase of all shares: the Buyer could pay the full price yet have substantially less protection if the Seller cannot transfer what it has sold. Similarly, a general warranty deadline may expire before tax exposures emerge. The proposed language applying limitations to “all Claims” also risks hollowing out the Ironquay indemnity and other negotiated protections.

**Push back:**

- Give title, ownership, authority and capacity warranties a **separate cap of at least the purchase price**, longer survival and no general de minimis or basket.
- Seek a standalone tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion tax, with an appropriate separate cap and period linked to applicable assessment and reassessment periods. Address pre-Completion periods that straddle Completion.
- Give specific indemnities separately negotiated scope, caps and time limits, without the general warranty thresholds or disclosure/knowledge qualifications unless expressly agreed.
- Ensure fraud and fraudulent concealment are expressly excluded from contractual caps, time limits and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions. Review any broader carve-outs for deliberate breach with counsel.

Check the actual definitions and cross-references throughout clauses 9, 12, 13 and 20: a headline carve-out will not help if another provision reimposes the limitation.

### Disclosure, knowledge and reliance

The Seller seeks to disclose the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records, while excluding claims for matters the Buyer or advisers knew **or could discover**. That could make the Buyer bear risks that were buried in documents, insufficiently explained or not actually understood. The specific disclosures also preserve uncertainty rather than establishing that each problem is resolved.

**Push back:**

- Permit disclosure against warranties only where a matter is **fairly disclosed in sufficient detail** to identify its nature and scope, with specific references to accessible documents. Reject blanket disclosure of the data room and public records.
- Delete “discoverable” knowledge. If any knowledge qualification is agreed, confine it to the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals after specified enquiries—not all advisers or constructive knowledge.
- Ensure disclosure and knowledge do not defeat specific indemnities, completion obligations, price adjustments or remedies for fraud.
- Narrow exclusive-remedy and non-reliance wording so it does not cut across the agreed express warranties, indemnities and other SPA remedies or the fraud carve-out.

Fair disclosure is not itself a cure. For issues already identified below, the Buyer should obtain the relevant consent, price protection or indemnity rather than rely solely on a warranty claim that may be disputed as disclosed.

## 2. Completion and purchase-price risks

### Bluefen consent — material customer concentration

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million, or 30%, of FY26 revenue**. The data room identifies a change-control consent and conditions, but contains neither final consent nor evidence that the conditions have been satisfied. A condition satisfied merely by delivery of written consent could allow Completion with an ineffective or conditional consent, or one carrying unacceptable commercial concessions.

**Push back:** Make Completion conditional on receipt of a valid, unconditional and effective Bluefen consent, **or consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer**, with the associated contractual conditions satisfied or validly waived. Require the Seller to use stronger, specified efforts, keep the Buyer informed and not agree adverse amendments without Buyer approval. Provide a long-stop date and Buyer termination right if the condition is not met. Review clauses 11.2 and 11.3 and the proposed consent itself.

### Riverlark facility — debt-free/cash-free delivery

Approximately **AUD 3.2 million** remains outstanding and no final discharge is included. A release after Completion exposes the Buyer to debt, encumbrance and execution risk, contrary to the debt-free/cash-free baseline.

**Push back:** Require, as simultaneous Completion steps:

- A current payout statement and binding discharge/release undertaking from Riverlark.
- Payment of the required payout **directly from Seller proceeds** under the Completion funds flow, with the Seller responsible for any shortfall.
- Release of all relevant security and guarantees, with evidence and registration steps required for discharge as applicable.
- A completion deliverable package and post-Completion cooperation for any administrative registration steps that cannot occur simultaneously.

The funds flow and price adjustment must avoid both leaving the Buyer with the debt and deducting the same debt twice. Verify accrued interest, break fees and other discharge costs.

### Completion bonuses — AUD 420,000 plus possible on-costs

The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, and are omitted from the draft funds flow. The Seller calling them “a matter for the Seller” does not allocate who pays if the Company becomes liable. Tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unconfirmed.

**Push back:** Establish the terms, beneficiaries, trigger dates and applicable on-costs. Allocate the full economic cost to the Seller through an express debt-like item or equivalent price deduction, or a Seller-funded payment mechanism, with protection for later crystallisation. Specify who administers payroll and when. Avoid double counting if a provision is already captured in completion accounts or working capital.

### Supplier renewals — AUD 330,000

The three related renewals total **AUD 330,000**, but the disclosures do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Neither automatic treatment as Seller debt nor acceptance as ordinary operating cost is justified on the current record.

**Push back:** Review DD-008 and DD-011 together, including dates, commitment, termination and benefit periods. Allocate any pre-Completion accrued or unavoidable Seller-period cost through the agreed debt/working-capital mechanics or a specific adjustment; do not deduct the same amount twice. Restrict new or accelerated commitments before Completion without Buyer consent.

## 3. Specific operational and IP risks

### Ironquay — ownership of SOW3 materials

Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of **every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but does not independently prove non-payment. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The current indemnity limited to that payment may not cover a failure of title, infringement allegations or the cost of replacing or securing rights.

**Push back:** Before Completion, verify the full amount due and payment status, obtain evidence of cleared payment and an executed confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory confirmation of rights. Review the underlying IP terms and whether all relevant materials and contributors are covered. Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from the identified ownership and payment issue, including reasonable enforcement, remediation and third-party claim costs, with its own adequate cap and survival period. Do not assert the AUD 180,000 is definitely unpaid without verification.

### Export/privacy incident

An export link went to an unintended external email address and may have contained approximately **1,240 records**. Access, scope, notification obligations and loss remain unknown; this is not established to be a confirmed breach. The uncertainty nevertheless creates potential investigation, notification, remediation and third-party exposure.

**Push back:** Require prompt completion and disclosure of a documented investigation, preservation of evidence, assessment of access and containment, and legal assessment of any notification duties. Restrict settlement or communications that prejudice the Buyer without appropriate consultation, while not delaying any legally required action. Seek a specific Seller indemnity for pre-Completion incident-related losses and reasonable investigation, response and remediation costs, with a separate cap and survival period. Consider an appropriate Completion condition or termination protection if findings establish a materially adverse exposure.

### IP and tax generally

The Seller regards both as settled under the general regime, but that regime is limited and the Ironquay issue illustrates the risk.

**Push back:** In addition to the specific protections above, review substantive warranties on ownership, licences, infringement, open-source use and data rights, as well as the tax covenant and warranties. Appropriate scope depends on the business and DD findings; do not assume a general IP warranty resolves a disclosed title defect.

## 4. Other diligence and interim actions

- **Share title:** DD-012 records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares; it is useful evidence, not conclusive independent verification of the entire capital position. Verify the register and supporting issuances/transfers, share structure, encumbrances, options and other rights. Require transfers and corporate approvals at Completion, plus fundamental warranties.
- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a **notification**, not a stated landlord-consent requirement. Confirm timing and content and assign responsibility for compliant notice; do not invent a consent condition.
- **Mossvale:** The disclosed restriction is on **assignment**, not expressly on a share sale. Check the full contract and transaction steps, including any deemed assignment or change-control language, before deciding whether consent is needed.
- **Pre-Completion conduct:** Require ordinary-course operation, appropriate controls on material contracts, debt and payments, and prompt notification of material developments. Align these obligations with the Bluefen, incident, bonus and renewal protections.

## Recommended negotiation priorities

| Priority | Buyer position |
|---|---|
| **Completion gates** | Effective Bluefen consent on acceptable terms; Riverlark repayment and security release at Completion. |
| **Value protection** | Allocate AUD 420,000 bonuses and applicable on-costs to Seller; determine treatment of the AUD 330,000 renewals; reconcile all items with the debt-free/cash-free mechanics and funds flow. |
| **Core remedies** | Separate fundamental, tax and specific-indemnity regimes from general caps, baskets and deadlines; express fraud carve-out. |
| **Disclosure and reliance** | Fair, specific disclosure only; delete discoverable-knowledge exclusion; preserve agreed contractual remedies. |
| **Known risks** | Obtain Ironquay payment/title evidence and broader indemnity; investigate and specifically protect against the export incident. |
| **Verification** | Check the complete SPA, underlying DD documents, share title and completion deliverables before signing or waiving conditions. |
